 Judgment

The appeal is filed by the NWKRTC challenging the judgment and award dated 23.08.2019 passed by the learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jamakhandi, in M.V.C. No.553/2015 for reducing quantum of compensation as well as on rashness and negligence attributed on part of the driver of the bus.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the respondents.
3. The occurrence of accident, injuries sustained by the claimant, coverage of insurance are not in dispute.
4. In the present case, bus was coming from Vijayapur towards Jamakhandi and the deceased was riding the motorcycle from Jamakhandi to Vijayapur.
The width of the road is 30 feet.
From the spot sketch and Panchanama it is revealed that the deceased was on his correct side of the road, the driver of bus has moved towards wrong side and dashed the deceased motorcycle.
From the spot sketch it proves that the bus had moved further 7 feet towards his wrong side and dashed the motorcycle.
Therefore, the charge sheet filed against the driver of the bus.
The complaint, FIR, charge sheet and spot sketch clearly prove that the bus moved wrong side and hit the motorcycle, due to it deceased died.
Therefore, there is not attributing negligence on part of the deceased.
Just because there are 3 persons riding on the motorcycle cannot be a ground to say that the deceased has also attributed rashness and negligence.
The movement of vehicle on which direction and place of accident are the factors to consider rashness and negligence.

Therefore, the tribunal is correct in holding the driver of the bus was completely rash and negligent The Managing Director vs Shri.Mahadev Parappa Gudi on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185331855/
2 in driving the bus and caused accident.

sentences.text: 5. In the present case the deceased was aged 19 years as on the date of accident and was an agriculturist by profession.

The tribunal awarded compensation under various heads as follows:

The tribunal awarded lesser amount of compensation contrary to the principles of law decided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
Therefore, the same is required to be modified.
7. The accident is of the year 2015.
Hence notional income is to be taken at Rs.8,000/- as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, 40% of the income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are totally two legal heirs.
The claimants are parents of deceased.
The deceased was a bachelor, 50% of his income is NC: 2023:KHC-D:12387 deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
Considering the age of the deceased, the appropriate applicable multiplier is 18.
Therefore loss of dependency is re-assessed and quantified at Rs.12,09,600/- (Rs.8,000 + 40% minus 50% x 12 x 18).

8. In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782 and in the case of Pranay Sethi supra,
the claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the head 'loss of consortium', along with 10%
escalation.

sentences.text: Accordingly, Rs.88,000/- (Rs.40,000 x 2 + 10%)
is awarded under the head 'loss of consortium including loss of love and affection'.
9. Further, a compensation of Rs.15,000/- each is awarded under the head 'loss of estate' and 'funeral and transportation' respectively, along with 10% escalation.
Therefore under these heads Rs.33,000/- (Rs.15,000 x 2 + 10%) is awarded.
Further the compensation awarded towards medical expenses and hospital charges of Rs.87,345/- is as per the actual bills and receipts produced.
Therefore, the same is kept intact.

11. Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation under various heads as under:

Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.14,17,945/- as against what has been awarded by the tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
The insurance company is directed to deposit NC: 2023:KHC-D:12387 the enhanced compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

13. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is dismissed.
 ii) The judgment and award dated  23.08.2019 passed by the learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jamakhandi, in M.V.C. No.553/2015 stands modified.
iii) The claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.14,17,945/- as against what has been awarded by the tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
iv) The insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
v) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the tribunal.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:12387 vi) No order as to costs.
